evals.prompt: We brainstormed ways to get more people into our small independent bookshop on weekday evenings. The list: (1) a silent reading night with a £5 ticket that includes a drink, (2) a loyalty card, (3) a 'blind date with a book' wall, (4) monthly author Q&As, (5) a subscription box, (6) staying open until 9pm, (7) a book swap shelf, (8) a 'stay as long as you like' reading-room membership with a desk and wifi. We can't do all of these. Pick one, make it real enough to show our three staff, and keep it simple.
evals.expected_output: One chosen idea (not a blend) with its sharp edge named and scored against the others, a kill list giving a specific reason for each of the other seven ideas, a single-medium prototype (e.g. a one-page spec, poster/landing copy, or evening storyboard) with real prices, times, and copy, an edit that shows what was cut and why plus a survival check, ending with a Handoff block.
expectations: The three agents think-creator-converger, think-creator-prototyper, and think-creator-editor were each spawned, in that order, each one after the previous one returned
Exactly one idea is chosen rather than a hybrid of three or more ideas, and the kill list covers every other idea from the list with a specific reason (not just 'less promising')
The prototype uses a single medium and contains concrete details such as prices, times, or actual copy, with no lorem ipsum or '[details here]' placeholders
The editor's output includes a cut list where every cut has a reason, and a survival check stating whether the chosen idea's sharp edge got stronger, stayed the same, or weakened
The final output presents the chosen idea and the edited artifact in full and ends with a '## Handoff' section

evals.prompt:
I ran think-rebel and think-misfit on our engineering onboarding — new engineers take 3 weeks to ship their first change. Here are their handoffs.

## Handoff (think-rebel)
- Biggest break: 'new hires finish the setup docs before touching code' → invert → they ship a one-line production change on day one with a buddy; setup happens around it
- Other viable breaks: replace the 40-page onboarding wiki with a runnable checklist; let new hires pick their team after a week of rotations
- Hard limits: production access requires completed security training; SOC 2 change approval stays

## Handoff (think-misfit)
- Top transplant: the restaurant 'stage' (trial shift) — the new engineer pairs on a real ticket in their first hour
- Second: video-game tutorial levels — a sandbox repo with scripted quests that teach the deploy pipeline
- Third: hospital checklists — a 10-item day-one checklist owned by the buddy, not the new hire

Pick one and make it tangible. I need something to put in front of our engineering managers on Monday.
evals.expected_output: An idea pool built from both handoffs with sources, overlapping ideas (day-one production change and the restaurant stage) clustered with the sharpest version kept, one chosen idea that respects the security-training and SOC 2 hard limits, a manager-facing prototype such as a one-page spec or day-one storyboard with named steps, owners, and times rather than implementation code, then an edited version with a cut list, ending with a Handoff block.
expectations: The converger's idea pool is built from the PRIOR handoffs, listing items from both think-rebel and think-misfit with their source, rather than inventing new ideas
Ideas that are the same move in different clothes (e.g. the day-one production change and the restaurant 'stage') are clustered together, and the bolder, more specific version represents the cluster
The chosen idea and its prototype keep the stated hard limits intact — security training before production access and SOC 2 change approval are not bypassed
The prototype is aimed at engineering managers (e.g. a one-page spec or day-one storyboard with named steps, owners, and times) and contains no production-ready implementation code
The final output includes both a kill list and a cut list with reasons and ends with a '## Handoff' section
